children: New Delhi, September 20 The Defence Research and Development Organisation’s (DRDO’s) first-of-production model (FOPM) for the 30 kW-class directed-energy weapon (DEW) — a strong arm of ‘Sudarshan Chakra’ comprehensive air defence system announced by Prime Minister  Narendra Modi earlier, will be available within a year to  counter swarm drones and UAVs .
The truck-mounted DEW uses electromagnetic energy for destroying targets either by way of soft kill or hard kill.

“Having demonstrated the technology,  DRDO will issue an express of interest in the next six months to select a production partner for the new 30 kW high energy laser beam weapon system,”  BK Das, Director General of Bengaluru-based DRDO lab Electronics and Communication Systems (ECS), said in an exclusive interaction with businessline. The technology trial was carried out last year.

“Within a year, we hope to see the FOPM. It will undergo further series of tests and trials to ascertain range and other parameters desired by users”, he said, explaining the cycle from the drawing board to shop floor.
This will be part of the the ‘OODA loop’, a decision-making military framework that stands for ‘Observe, Orient, Decide, and Act.’
The DEW is emerging as a strong arm of the multiple approach of neutralisation where choice of weapon, be it kinetic or non-kinetic, is conditioned on the incoming projectiles, as per the DG of ECS.

Speaking on the overarching country-wide air defence system Sudarsh Chakra,  Das said it’s a great vision by the Prime Minister and the country needs it. We have most of the ingredients in some form or the other in our ecosystem. We need to integrate all of them for effective layered defence system.” In the entire push, private industry, MSMEs and start-ups are deeply involved.

This is the third in the series of DEWs developed indigenously by the DRDO, orbiting India into a select few club of countries like, US, China, Russia, Israel, UK and Germany, that possess such non-kinetic capabilities, gaining relevance in the modern battlefield defined by economics of warfare.

India had deployed DRDO’s 2kW DEW along the Line of Control (LoC) in Operation Sindoor as part of multi-layered inner-tier air defence network to counter asymmetric aerial threats from Pakistan over a range of up to 1 km. The DRDO had selected multiple production partners including Bharat Electronics Ltd, and Adani Defence & Aerospace.

The more potent version of 10 kW DEW can engage drones, UAVs and sensors within a range of 1.5 km to 2 km. The Defence Acquisition Council, chaired by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, has issued Acceptance of Necessity (which in principal approval) for 10 to 12 numbers of 10 kW DEW which will be subsumed into the Integrated Drone Detection and Interdiction System (IDD&IS) Mark-2.
Now the development-cum-production partner, L&T, has to come up with (FOPM) of 10 kW class DEW and subsequent to that it will for further trials, the DG leading scientist stated.

title: DRDO’s 30 kW directed-energy weapon to be ready within a year to counter swarm drones
